title: Energy, Work and Power Module 2 Lesson 2: Smooth Conservation Mechanical Energy custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from a height of $7.2\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. Assuming no air resistance, use conservation of mechanical energy to calculate the speed of the particle immediately before it hits the ground. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A block of mass $0.8\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up a line of greatest slope of a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Calculate the maximum vertical height reached before coming to instantaneous rest. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A child on a sledge starts from rest at the top of a smooth hill of vertical height $12.8\text{ m}$. Calculate the speed of the sledge when it reaches the bottom of the hill. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A small bead of mass $0.25\text{ kg}$ slides along a smooth curved wire. It passes point $A$ with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Point $B$ on the wire is $1.8\text{ m}$ vertically below point $A$. Calculate the speed of the bead as it passes $B$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A pendulum bob of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at a position where it is $0.45\text{ m}$ vertically above its lowest point. Calculate its kinetic energy and speed as it passes through its lowest point. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A puck of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up a line of greatest slope of a smooth plane inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal. Calculate the distance the puck travels along the plane before coming to instantaneous rest. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

questions.prompt: A trolley of mass $4\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at the top of a smooth plane inclined at $24^\circ$ to the horizontal. The trolley slides down a line of greatest slope through a distance of $18\text{ m}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the vertical height lost by the trolley, and find the loss in gravitational potential energy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State the kinetic energy of the trolley at the bottom of the plane, and calculate its speed at the bottom.

questions.prompt: A skateboarder of mass $60\text{ kg}$ starts from rest at the rim of a smooth curved half-pipe ramp at a vertical height of $4.5\text{ m}$ above the lowest point. The skateboarder rolls freely without any resistance down to the bottom and then ascends the opposite side. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use conservation of mechanical energy to calculate the speed of the skateboarder at the lowest point of the ramp.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the skateboarder when ascending the opposite side at a height of $2.5\text{ m}$ above the lowest point.

questions.prompt: A rollercoaster car of mass $500\text{ kg}$ passes over the crest of a smooth track at point $A$ with a speed of $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Point $A$ is $24\text{ m}$ above the ground. The car descends into a dip at point $B$, which is $4\text{ m}$ above the ground, and then rises to a second crest at point $C$, which is $16\text{ m}$ above the ground. Assume all resistive forces are negligible. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy of the car at point $A$ taking the ground level as zero potential energy, and find the speed of the car at point $B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the car at point $C$, and calculate the ratio of the kinetic energy of the car at $B$ to its kinetic energy at $C$.

questions.prompt: A small block of mass $2\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at point $P$ at the top of a smooth slope inclined at $40^\circ$ to the horizontal. The block slides $10\text{ m}$ down this slope to point $Q$. At $Q$, the slope smoothly transitions into a second incline at an angle of $15^\circ$ to the horizontal without loss of kinetic energy. The block travels a further distance $s$ along this second slope before reaching horizontal ground at point $R$, where its speed is $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the vertical height of point $P$ above point $Q$, and find the speed of the block as it passes point $Q$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use conservation of mechanical energy across the entire descent from $P$ to $R$ to find the total vertical height of $P$ above $R$, and hence determine the distance $s$ travelled along the second slope.

questions.prompt: A light inextensible string of length $2.4\text{ m}$ has one end attached to a fixed point $O$. A particle of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ is attached to the other end. The particle is held with the taut string making an angle of $60^\circ$ with the downward vertical through $O$ and is released from rest. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the vertical distance the particle falls as it swings to the downward vertical, and find its speed at the lowest point of its swing.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By considering energy conservation, find the speed of the particle when the string makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the downward vertical, and explain why the tension in the string does no work during the motion.

questions.prompt: A ski jumper of mass $72\text{ kg}$ starts from rest at point $A$ at the top of a smooth in-run ramp at a height of $50\text{ m}$ above the landing bowl. The ramp descends smoothly to a low dip at point $B$, $10\text{ m}$ above the bowl, before curving upwards to the take-off lip at point $C$, which is $18\text{ m}$ above the bowl. The skier launches into the air from point $C$. Resistive forces on the ramp are negligible. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the ski jumper at point $B$ and at the take-off lip $C$, and find the change in kinetic energy between $B$ and $C$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: After launching from point $C$, the ski jumper flies through the air under gravity alone and lands at point $D$ in the landing bowl, where the vertical height is $0\text{ m}$. Use energy conservation to find the landing speed of the skier at $D$, and calculate the percentage of total mechanical energy at launch that was kinetic energy.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $8\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $u = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ down an inclined plane of length $25\text{ m}$ inclined at $18^\circ$ to the horizontal. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Assuming the plane is perfectly smooth, use the principle of conservation of mechanical energy to calculate the speed of the block at the bottom of the plane.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: In reality, the plane is rough with coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.15$. Calculate the normal contact force and work done against friction over the $25\text{ m}$ descent, and determine the actual speed of the block at the bottom of the rough plane, comparing it with the smooth speed from part (a).
